title: Best Datacenter Proxies for Scraping in 2026: 5 Providers Priced
desc: Best datacenter proxies for scraping in 2026: Webshare, Decodo, IPRoyal, Oxylabs and Bright Data priced from their own pages, fair use caps and refunds.
keywords: best datacenter proxies, best datacenter proxies for scraping, datacenter proxy providers 2026, cheap datacenter proxies, dedicated datacenter proxies, shared datacenter proxies, datacenter proxy pricing
body:
Quick answer: The best datacenter proxies for scraping in 2026 depend on what you are buying. For a fixed handful of datacenter IPs, Webshare is the cheapest credible option, at $2.99 a month for 100 shared proxies and 10 free ones to start. For dedicated IPs on a budget, IPRoyal is $1.39 per IP on a 90 day term, and Oxylabs' three IP minimum at $6.75 plus five free IPs is the lowest entry ticket to a tier one provider. For scale, geography and a catalogue that goes beyond proxies, Bright Data is the one we use, at $1.40 per shared IP for 10 or $0.42 per GB at 5 TB. We priced all five providers from their own pages on September 5, 2026, and every one of them advertises a floor you cannot buy at the entry tier.

Datacenter proxies: what you are actually buying

A datacenter proxy is an IP address that belongs to a hosting company rather than a home internet connection. That makes it fast, stable and cheap, and it also makes it the easiest kind of proxy for a website to detect, because the whole subnet is visibly commercial. Every provider on this list says a version of the same thing in its own FAQ: use datacenter IPs for targets without serious anti bot systems, such as price monitoring, SERP checks, most public directories and your own applications, and switch to residential or an unblocker for protected sites. Decodo's FAQ is the bluntest: datacenter proxies on Shopify are "sitting ducks".

Providers sell the same product on three meters. Per IP, shared is the cheapest, and the IP is used by other customers. Per IP, dedicated is yours alone and costs two to ten times more. Per GB gives you rotation across a large pool and charges for traffic. Every per IP plan that says "unlimited bandwidth" carries a fair use cap, and the cap is usually 100 GB per IP per month.

Webshare: cheapest shared IPs, 10 free

Webshare's datacenter product is called Proxy Server, and its entry price is not a trick: 10 proxies free, forever, then 100 shared proxies for $2.99 a month, 1,000 for $29.90 ($26.91 on annual billing), 5,000 for $149.50 and 60,000 for $1,794. The checkout for the 100 proxy plan carries a 250 GB bandwidth allowance, so the cap is on traffic rather than per IP. Private proxies (one user per IP, Webshare's term) run $0.30 per IP from 20 IPs at $6, and dedicated proxies are listed at $0.77 per IP. The meta description's "from $0.018/IP" is the 60,000 proxy annual rate; the page's real entry price is $0.03 per IP, which is still the lowest on this list by a wide margin. What you give up: a smaller published pool and less granular targeting than the tier one vendors. For a scraper that hits unprotected sites and needs a few hundred rotating addresses, this is where we start.

Decodo: the cleanest per GB ladder, 14 day refund

Decodo, formerly Smartproxy, sells datacenter three ways and prints all three honestly on one comparison table: pay per GB from $0.60 (10 GB for $6) down to $0.45 (1 TB for $450), pay per IP from $0.10 per IP with a 100 IP minimum plus a traffic allowance, and dedicated from $2.50 per IP in only four locations, the US, UK, Germany and Japan. It is also the only provider here with a plain money back window, 14 days. The one thing to catch: the navigation says datacenter "from $0.02/IP", the comparison table says pay per IP "from $0.10/IP", and the $0.02 is the volume end of a ladder the page does not show. Shared IPs come from a 100,000 plus pool with 18 countries listed across the Americas, Europe and APAC.

IPRoyal: dedicated only, priced by term length

IPRoyal does not sell shared datacenter IPs at all, which is a deliberate position and a good one if you need addresses nobody else is burning. Its dedicated proxies are $1.57 per IP on a 30 day term, $1.48 on 60 days and $1.39 on 90 days, with state and city targeting, 60 plus locations, HTTP(S) and SOCKS5, and a published 100 GB per IP monthly allowance pooled across the order, after which speed is reduced rather than access cut. The "from $1.39/proxy" in the navigation is the 90 day price; the month to month price is $1.57. That is still cheaper than a dedicated IP from Bright Data ($2.20 at 10 IPs), Oxylabs ($2.25) or Decodo ($2.50), so for a dedicated address on a budget IPRoyal is the number to beat. We priced its residential network in best proxies for web scraping, where the term length qualifier was the same story.

Oxylabs: five free IPs and a three IP minimum

Oxylabs is the easiest tier one provider to try: five free datacenter IPs on signup, then dedicated at $2.25 per IP from 3 IPs ($6.75 a month) across 188 countries from a 1.9 million IP pool, shared per IP at $1.20 from 10 IPs ($12), and shared per GB at $0.59 from 20 GB ($11.80) up to 2 TB. Self service plans are refundable within three days if you have used under 20 percent. The navigation's "from $0.70/IP" did not appear on the pricing page at any quantity up to 3,000, so treat $1.20 shared and $2.25 dedicated as the real entry prices. If you want a tier one vendor's support, uptime page and compliance material for a small job, this is the cheapest way in.

Bright Data: three meters, the biggest pool, the widest catalogue

Bright Data's datacenter page, updated September 1, 2026, sells a 1.3 million IP pool on all three meters: shared $1.40 per IP for 10 IPs ($14) down to $0.90 at 1,000, dedicated $2.20 down to $1.30, and per GB at $0.60 pay as you go down to $0.42 on the 5 TB, $1,999 plan. Fair use is 100 GB per IP per month, pooled. Two cautions from its own page: the navigation's "from $0.90/IP" is the 1,000 IP rate, and the meta description's "starting from $0.077/GB" does not appear anywhere on the page. Two reasons we still buy it: country targeting and a support and compliance stack that satisfies enterprise clients, and the fact that the same account gives you Web Unlocker (5,000 free requests a month) and the SERP and Scraper APIs for the sites where datacenter IPs stop working. Full ladders are in our Bright Data pricing guide.

Check Bright Data datacenter pricing

Side by side: 10 IPs, 100 IPs and 100 GB

  • 10 shared IPs: Webshare $0 (free tier), Oxylabs $12, Bright Data $14. Decodo requires 100 IPs on the per IP plan.
  • 100 shared IPs: Webshare $2.99, Decodo about $10 at the $0.10 rate before traffic, Oxylabs $120, Bright Data $100.
  • 10 dedicated IPs: IPRoyal $15.70 month to month or $13.90 on 90 days, Bright Data $22, Oxylabs $22.50, Decodo $25.
  • 100 GB of shared traffic: Decodo $54, Oxylabs $59, Bright Data $60 pay as you go. Webshare's 100 proxy plan includes 250 GB for $2.99.

The spread on shared IPs is 40 to 1 between Webshare and the tier one vendors, and it is real. The spread on dedicated IPs is under 2 to 1. The spread on per GB traffic is almost nothing. So the buying rule is simple: if you need cheap shared addresses, the tier one premium buys you nothing you can measure; if you need dedicated addresses or traffic, pick on support, refund policy and geography, because the prices are within a few dollars.

How to choose in 2026

  • Read the card, not the menu. Five of five providers here quote a navigation price that is a volume or long term rate. Webshare $0.018, Decodo $0.02, IPRoyal $1.39, Oxylabs $0.70, Bright Data $0.90: none is the entry price.
  • Find the fair use line. 100 GB per IP is the norm, pooled across the order. Divide your monthly traffic by that before you decide per IP is cheaper than per GB.
  • Match the meter to the bottleneck. Fixed identities need dedicated IPs; rotation needs per GB; a few hundred cheap addresses for unprotected targets need shared.
  • Know when to stop. If success rates on a target drop below 90 percent, you are paying for retries; move that target to residential or an unblocker rather than buying more datacenter IPs.

The part that no proxy vendor sells is the pipeline: what gets scraped, how it is cleaned, and how it reaches your CRM or your outreach tool. That is the job we do in lead generation and AI automation engagements, on whichever of these five providers fits the client's budget, with the email infrastructure to send from once the data lands.

faqs: What is the cheapest datacenter proxy provider in 2026?

For shared IPs, Webshare: 10 free proxies, then 100 for $2.99 a month with a 250 GB allowance, as of September 5, 2026. For dedicated IPs, IPRoyal at $1.57 per IP month to month or $1.39 on a 90 day term. For traffic billed per GB, Decodo at $0.60 down to $0.45, Oxylabs at $0.59 and Bright Data at $0.60 down to $0.42 are within a few cents of each other.
Are datacenter proxies good for web scraping?

For unprotected targets, yes, and they are the fastest and cheapest option. For sites with anti bot systems they are easy to detect because the whole IP range is visibly commercial; Decodo's own FAQ calls them sitting ducks on Shopify. Use datacenter IPs for price monitoring, SERP checks and public directories, and move protected targets to residential proxies or an unblocker such as Bright Data's Web Unlocker.
What does unlimited bandwidth mean on a per IP datacenter plan?

It means a fair use allowance, typically 100 GB per IP per month pooled across the order. Bright Data and IPRoyal both state that figure. Above it, Bright Data says additional charges may apply and IPRoyal reduces speed. If your job is traffic heavy, compare the per GB plans instead, where the three tier one vendors are priced within $0.01 of each other.

Shared IPs are used by other customers and cost from $0.03 per IP at Webshare to $1.40 at Bright Data. Dedicated IPs are yours alone and cost $1.39 to $2.50 per IP. Choose dedicated when you need a stable identity, for example account management or long running sessions, and shared when you need many cheap addresses for simple data collection.
Which datacenter proxy providers offer a free trial or refund?

Webshare gives 10 free proxies permanently. Oxylabs gives five free datacenter IPs and refunds self service plans within three days if under 20 percent is used. Decodo offers a 14 day money back window. Bright Data has no free datacenter tier but offers 5,000 free Web Unlocker requests a month and matches a first deposit up to $500. IPRoyal's shortest commitment is a 30 day term.
Why do the advertised prices differ from what I am charged?

Because every provider on this list quotes its best volume or longest term rate in the navigation. Webshare's $0.018 is the 60,000 proxy annual rate, Decodo's $0.02 is a volume rate not shown on the page, IPRoyal's $1.39 is the 90 day price, Oxylabs' $0.70 did not appear on its page, and Bright Data's $0.90 is the 1,000 IP rate. Price from the plan card at your actual quantity.
